contradiction_quotes.text: we programmatically instantiate patient- and population-level queries over MIMIC-IV 3.1
The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)

rationale: S1 names MIMIC-IV, version 3.1, PhysioNet and the 2008-2019 collection window, but S1-S3 give no route from a task to its source record; the task-to-source-record claim appears only in S4 code comments, which do not count. Scored 1. The S4 comment states MIMIC-IV 2.2 while S1 states 3.1, so a contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
the source institution's review board determined that the study qualified for a waiver of consent
The data are released under a credentialed-access data use agreement

rationale: S1 states origin, collection context, the credentialed-access data use agreement, and an IRB determination with a consent waiver. All four required elements are present.

quotes.text: against the U.S. adult inpatient population reported in a national hospital discharge survey

rationale: The appendix compares age, sex and race distributions of benchmark patients against a named target population, the U.S. adult inpatient population in a national discharge survey.

quotes.text: Safety testing identifies unsafe outputs like contraindicated medications; bias testing compares accuracy across different patient demographics.

rationale: S1 states that both an unsafe-output test suite and a bias test suite are built into the benchmark. Scored 2 on the reported statement; no results for these suites appear elsewhere in the packet.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.
we measured verbatim overlap between the test tasks and a public web corpus, finding no exact matches

rationale: Developer-side controls are stated (held-out split, gated access, canary), plus a measured verbatim-overlap check with a result. This meets the control-plus-measured-check anchor.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: S1 states that the agent cannot reach ground-truth answers at run time and names the mechanisms: no network path from the sandbox and labels not published in the repository.

quotes.text: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions
GPT-5.2 (high) ( OpenAI, 2025b ) performs this verification.

rationale: Data and software are stated as pinned. However, S1 also says the outcome verification is performed by GPT-5.2 (high), an external API judge identified without a snapshot ID, which conflicts with the claim of no external call other than the model under test. The judge is therefore live or unpinned, giving 1.

searched: S1 (task construction, reproducibility statement, appendix excerpts), S2 (no chunks), S3 (no chunks), S4 (notes.py), S5 (no chunks). No scripted reference solution run through the grader, and no manual or agent-based solvability evidence, is reported.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.

rationale: Some actions write state, so NA does not apply. Unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised, but the packet does not state that the grader checks unchanged state generally, and most tasks are read-only. Scored as partial.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks, and the chance success rate for each metric is reported in the appendix.

rationale: S1 reports an empirical random-agent rate and states per-metric chance rates. The S4 comment gives a different random rate (2.5% on 120 tasks) but does not oppose the reported property, so it is not flagged.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: S1 reports a random-action agent's success over the benchmark's tasks. The do-nothing result appears only in S4 comments, which do not count.

quotes.text: 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%

rationale: The benchmark validated its automatic evaluator on its own outputs against physician labels and reports agreement and both error rates.

quotes.text: with temperature 0 and 2,048-token output ceiling
Repeated-run evaluation further shows that pass^k consistency, which requires all k attempts to succeed, falls below 50% for most evaluated models at k=4

rationale: S1 states temperature 0 and a repeated-run evaluation protocol with k=4 (protocol detailed in an appendix per the reproducibility statement). S4 gives three runs per task, which differs from k=4, but that is treated as a different context and not flagged.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task

rationale: S1 states 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for the reported results, covering the model comparisons. No Table 3 interval values appear in the excerpt, so this rests on the stated reporting.

quotes.text: falls below 50% for most evaluated models at k=4
with temperature 0 and 2,048-token output ceiling

rationale: A run count of k=4 is stated for the repeated-run evaluation and temperature 0 with an output ceiling is stated. Independence of runs is not stated, so 2 of 3 elements are present.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: CIs are reported, the resampling unit (task) is named, and patient clustering is addressed by resampling patients. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: pass^k consistency, which requires all k attempts to succeed, falls below 50% for most evaluated models at k=4

rationale: A pass^k all-runs metric is reported with its run count (k=4). No action-level or state-level agreement across reruns is reported.

quotes.text: with temperature 0 and 2,048-token output ceiling
All reported results match harness version v1.2.0.

rationale: Dated or snapshot IDs are given for several evaluated models (e.g. gpt-4.1-2025-04-14), decoding parameters are stated, and a harness version is stated as matching the reported results. Caveat: the stated snapshot IDs gpt-4o and claude-3-5-sonnet do not correspond to the evaluated model list, and GPT-5.4 and Sonnet 4.6 have no snapshot ID.

quotes.text: The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.

rationale: The agent uses SQL/Python execution tools, so NA does not apply. Only element (ii) is shown, as write actions are identified in a table. No tool schema or error-return semantics appear in S1-S3. Whether this classification reaches the agent-visible surface cannot be told, since S5 has no chunks.

quotes.text: Completed trajectories are evaluated with a shared outcome verifier that checks answer correctness on Clean questions
abstention must be justified by evidence obtained during interaction
200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%

rationale: The grader input is the trajectory and answer, judged by an LLM (GPT-5.2). The rationale for trajectory-level grading is that abstention must be evidence-justified, and validation on 200 human-labelled outputs with per-class error rates is reported. The rationale element is the weakest of the three.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: S1 states controls on web and retrieval leakage, a private held-out split with hidden labels off all public surfaces, and a canary string on released tasks.

quotes.text: Model | Method | Demographics | Vitals | Medications | Cost | Labs | Diagnoses

rationale: Results are reported per clinical intent (a named benchmark axis). No results per patient subgroup are reported even though source records hold demographic fields (the Demographics column is an intent, not a subgroup), and no per-slice n is given.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
Access to the underlying records remains subject to the original MIMIC-IV credentialing and data use requirements.

rationale: Records are stated as real and de-identified, governance is stated (credentialed access, DUA, de-identification processing, IRB waiver), and redistribution terms for released data artifacts are stated separately from code.
